In 1907, Dr. Alzheimer published a treatise about a disease that would later be named after him.
Dr. Creutzfeldt and Dr. Jakob were colleagues of Dr. Alzheimer and identified a similar brain-wasting disease.

Mad Cow Disease causes the brains of cows to turn into a sponge-like mass.
The human variant of Mad Cow Disease is called Creutzfeldt Jakob Disease, or CJD.
The protein causing CJD does not contain DNA and is described as resembling a crystal.
Heat of 1000 degrees Fahrenheit does not destroy the protein particle associated with CJD.
The incubation period for CJD can last from one month to thirty years after infection.
CJD leads to a spongioform encephalitic condition that physically debilitates infected individuals.
Symptoms of CJD include cognitive impairment, ataxia, visual distortions, delirium, myoclonus, dysarthria, and profound dementia that can lead to death.
